title: Learner & New Driver Rules
whatItIs: Learners must meet extra rules while they learn, and new drivers face a lower points limit for their first 2 years.

keyFacts.text: Your supervisor MUST be at least 21 and have held a full licence for that type of car for at least 3 years.
L plates (or D plates in Wales) MUST be shown on the front and back of the car.
Learners MUST NOT drive on motorways unless with an approved driving instructor in a dual-control car.
A supervisor MUST NOT use a hand-held phone while supervising: the phone law applies to them too.

keyFacts: New drivers who get 6 or more points within 2 years of passing lose their licence.

items.title: Supervisor
items.text: Aged 21 or over, with a full licence for 3 years or more.

items.title: L or D plates
items.text: Front and back of the car while you are learning.

items.title: Motorways
items.text: Only with an approved driving instructor in a dual-control car.

items.title: Insurance
items.text: You must be insured to drive the car you learn in.

items.title: P plates
items.text: Optional after you pass. They show you are a new driver.

items.title: 6 points in 2 years
items.text: A new driver who reaches 6 points loses their licence.

a.label: L plates
points: D plates can be used in Wales

b.label: P plates
points: Show you are a new driver

onTheTest.question: Who may supervise a learner driver in a car?
options: Someone aged 21+ who has held a full licence for 3 years
Any full licence holder aged 18 or over
Someone aged 21+ who has held a licence for 1 year
Anyone who is insured to drive the car
onTheTest.why: A supervisor must be at least 21 and have held a full licence for that type of vehicle for at least 3 years.

traps: A learner can't go on a motorway with a parent, only with an instructor.
D plates are the Welsh version of L plates.
New drivers: 6 points within 2 years means a new provisional licence and passing theory and practical tests again.
